# @zakkster/lite-adaptive

Version: 1.7.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A zero-dependency, zero-GC family of APPROXIMATE, sublinear-space streaming
summaries over the TIME / RECENCY axis -- one small structure per question you can
only answer about the RECENT or CHANGING stream (sliding-window count / sum, drift,
decay), never the whole of it. It WITNESSES its RECENCY: every member proves its
MEASURED windowed error against the paper's THEORETICAL bound, next to the memory it
saves. It is the fourth corner of the suite -- @zakkster/lite-o1 is EXACT O(1),
@zakkster/lite-filter is approximate MEMBERSHIP, @zakkster/lite-sketch is CUMULATIVE
approximate aggregates, and lite-adaptive is the WINDOWED / DECAYED / drift complement
(cumulative -> lite-sketch; recency -> lite-adaptive).

v0.1.0 ships the reference member -- ExponentialHistogram (sliding-window count / sum)
-- plus the shared time-source + fixed bucket-pool substrate. v0.2.0 adds ADWIN
(concept-drift detection + adaptive windowing). v0.3.0 adds ForwardDecay (time-decayed
count / sum / mean / rate; Cormode-Shkapenyuk-Srivastava-Xu, ICDE 2009) -- smooth
exponential decay in O(1) space (two scalar accumulators, no pool), EXACT modulo FP via
a periodic landmark rebase. v0.4.0 adds HeavyKeeper (decayed / windowed heavy hitters --
the top-k keys dominating the stream RIGHT NOW; Gong et al., USENIX ATC 2018) and a zero-box
`ADWIN.addFrom(buf, i)`. The four-member roster is now COMPLETE: ExponentialHistogram (0.1.0)
-> ADWIN (0.2.0, drift) -> ForwardDecay (0.3.0, decay) -> HeavyKeeper (0.4.0, decayed top-k)
-> 1.0.0 (API freeze, no new member). v1.1.0 adds the FIRST additive post-1.0 member --
SlidingHyperLogLog (windowed DISTINCT-count; how many distinct keys in the last W, in fixed space
at HLL accuracy; Chabchoub-Hebrail, 2010) -- via an LFPM ring (a per-register monotonic deque)
over the register bank. It is a PURE APPEND: the four frozen core classes stay BYTE-IDENTICAL
(only the file header + VERSION change). The time-based members (ExponentialHistogram,
ForwardDecay, SlidingHyperLogLog) and the item-based members (ADWIN, HeavyKeeper) each expose a
zero-box `addFrom(buf, i)` for callers whose inputs are read from a Float64Array. Members are
tree-shakeable named exports; prior members stay byte-identical on append (only the header +
VERSION change). v1.2.0 adds DriftDetector (scalar Page-Hinkley / CUSUM change detection). v1.3.0 adds
SlidingDDSketch (windowed relative-error QUANTILES over the last W; Masson-Rim-Lee, VLDB 2019, over a
fixed-(B+1) pane ring) -- the recency sibling of lite-sketch's cumulative DDSketch and the quantile
complement of SlidingHyperLogLog. Each post-1.0 member is a PURE APPEND: the prior classes stay
BYTE-IDENTICAL (only the file header + VERSION change). v1.4.0 adds advance(now) / advanceFrom(buf, i)
to the three TIME-windowed members (ExponentialHistogram, SlidingHyperLogLog, SlidingDDSketch) -- the
R11 idle-slide sweep (ADR 0009): move the window forward WITHOUT inserting a value, so an idle stream
still slides to empty with no traffic. EXPLICIT-time only, 0 B/op, every existing method byte-identical.
v1.5.0 adds SlidingCountMin (windowed per-label FREQUENCY over the last W; Cormode-Muthukrishnan, 2005,
over a fixed-(B+1) pane ring) -- the recency sibling of lite-sketch's cumulative CountMinSketch and the
frequency complement of SlidingHyperLogLog / SlidingDDSketch. It is a PURE APPEND: the seven prior
classes stay BYTE-IDENTICAL (only the file header + VERSION change). v1.6.0 adds DecayedReservoir (a
recency-biased fixed-k SAMPLE of actual stream values; Efraimidis-Spirakis A-Res weighted reservoir
over ForwardDecay weights, 2005/2009; ADR 0011) -- the sampling complement to ForwardDecay: where FD
gives decayed AGGREGATES exactly, DecayedReservoir gives a decayed SAMPLE from which the caller
computes ANY statistic. It is a SAMPLE, not a hard window, so (like ForwardDecay) it has NO advance().
It is a PURE APPEND: the eight prior classes stay BYTE-IDENTICAL (only the file header + VERSION
change). This completes the confirmed post-1.0 roadmap.

## Exports (from the single main file Adaptive.js)

- `ExponentialHistogram` -- class. A zero-GC sliding-window COUNT / SUM summary over a
  preallocated pool of `(timestamp, size)` buckets grouped by level (Datar-Gionis-Indyk-
  Motwani, SODA 2002). `add(now)` / `add(now, value)` is amortized O(1), 0 B/op -- it
  opens a level-0 bucket, merges the two oldest at any level that exceeds
  `k = ceil(1/(2*epsilon)) + 1` (a bounded cascade), and expires buckets older than
  `now - W`. Driven by a caller-supplied MONOTONE time source; the member never reads
  the wall clock. `count()` / `query()` are COLD windowed estimates within a HARD
  relative error `<= epsilon`; `sum()` error is bounded absolutely by half the oldest
  straddling bucket's value-mass (relative `<= epsilon` only for count / near-constant
  values -- F17). DGIM (the 0/1 count stream) is the `value = 1`
  special case. Fail closed on a bad W / epsilon (throws before allocation), a mode
  switch, a non-finite / decreasing `now`, or a non-positive value; queries never throw.
- `ADWIN` -- class. A zero-GC concept-drift detector with NO fixed window size (Bifet-
  Gavalda, SDM 2007). It keeps the most-recent values in an EH-style bucket list over its
  OWN variance-carrying `(sum, sumSq, count)` columns (design-parity with EH, a SEPARATE
  fixed pool). `add(x) -> boolean` appends a finite real (|x| <= sqrt(MAX_VALUE)/2, 1.7.0 F9), compresses buckets (at most 5 per
  level), scans every bucket-boundary split of the window into an older `W0` and a newer
  `W1` with the ADWIN2 variance-aware (Bernstein) cut, and on a detected mean shift DROPS
  the older sub-window -- returning `true` on the detecting item. Amortized O(1), 0 B/op
  incl. the cut-scan + the drop-older shrink. The window GROWS while the stream is stable
  and SHRINKS to the new concept on a change; the stationary false-alarm rate is bounded by
  `delta`. Item-indexed (no clock). `mean` / `variance` / `width` report the current
  adaptive window. Fail closed on a bad delta (throws before allocation); a non-finite `x`
  is a byte-identical no-op; getters never throw (0 on empty). `addFrom(buf, i) -> boolean`
  is a zero-box sibling of `add(x)` (reads `x = buf[i]` unboxed; same drift flag), for a
  caller whose fractional `x` would box at a non-inlined boundary.
- `ForwardDecay` -- class. A zero-GC, O(1)-space time-decayed COUNT / SUM / MEAN / RATE
  summary (Cormode-Shkapenyuk-Srivastava-Xu, ICDE 2009). Each element's weight decays
  exponentially with its AGE (halves every `halfLife` time units), measured FORWARD from a
  fixed landmark, so a weight is computed once at insert and never revised (the numeric-
  stability edge over backward decay). Two scalar accumulators `C` (decayed count) + `Sv`
  (decayed weighted sum) are maintained incrementally; a periodic alloc-free landmark rebase
  keeps them finite while the decayed aggregate stays EXACT modulo FP. `add(now?, value?)`
  is 0 B/op INCLUDING the rebase branch. Driven by a caller-supplied MONOTONE `now` (or
  count mode when omitted); accepts ANY finite real value (signed -- it contributes to the
  decayed sum / mean but counts as one decayed event). `count()` / `sum()` / `mean()` /
  `rate()` are O(1) queries at an optional query time. Fail closed on a bad halfLife (throws
  before allocation), a mode switch, a non-finite / decreasing `now`, or a non-finite value;
  a query time before the last add throws (can't un-decay); otherwise queries never throw
  (0 on empty).
- `HeavyKeeper` -- class. A zero-GC decayed / windowed TOP-K (heavy hitters right now; Gong
  et al., USENIX ATC 2018). A `d x w` table of `(fingerprint, count)` cells (SoA `Uint32Array`
  columns) + an intrusive top-k min-forest (design-parity with lite-o1 `FreqO1`, never a dep).
  `add(key, weight = 1) -> this` hashes `key` to `d` cells via an inline two-lane hash; a
  matching fingerprint adds the weight, a colliding one is DECAYED with probability `b^(-count)`
  (a seeded xorshift32 draw) and evicted at count 0 -- so cold keys erode and the top-k tracks
  the CURRENT concept. Amortized O(1), 0 B/op incl. the decay draw + the forest sift.
  `estimate(key)` is the max matching cell (0 for an unseen but VALID key; a non-safe-integer key
  -> NaN, never throws -- F12); `forEach(fn)` iterates the current top-k allocation-free; `topKInto(buf)`
  packs the current top-k into a caller Float64Array as [key, estimate] pairs (2 floats per entry)
  and returns the entry count, 0-alloc (buf length must be >= 2*k, else it throws);
  `topK()` is a COLD convenience that may allocate. `addFrom(buf, i)` is the zero-box entry
  (`key = buf[i]`, `weight = buf[i+1]` -- a large u32 key would box as a plain argument). Weight
  is an integer in [1, 2^32-1] (rank by count, total time, bytes, ...; a single over-range weight
  throws -- F10 -- while an ACCUMULATED cell SATURATES at 2^32-1, parity with SlidingCountMin).
  Keys are safe integers; on add/addFrom a bad key/weight/buffer throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first
  (byte-identical no-op), while the estimate query never throws (bad key -> NaN). Far lower error
  than Space-Saving on skewed / evolving streams. No `merge` (it decays natively). Getters:
  `d` / `w` / `k` / `b` / `seed` / `bytes` / `size`.
- `SlidingHyperLogLog` -- class. A zero-GC WINDOWED distinct-count (how many DISTINCT keys in the
  LAST W; Chabchoub-Hebrail, 2010) -- the RECENCY sibling of lite-sketch's cumulative HyperLogLog.
  An `m = 2^p` register bank where each register keeps a small FIXED LFPM ring of `(timestamp, rho)`
  entries (a monotonic deque, strictly decreasing rho). `add(now, key) -> this` (count mode via
  `add(undefined, key)`) derives register + rho from an inline two-lane hash, pops dominated tail
  entries, then drops expired heads (`stamp <= now - W`), and appends -- 0 B/op incl. the windowed
  eviction; a ring still full AFTER expiry drops its oldest entry and bumps `overflows` (`degraded`
  flips true -- the honest degradation signal, query-independent since expiry lives in add). Since
  1.7.0 (F8) expiry happens in add/addFrom, not the query. `addFrom(buf, i)` is
  the zero-box entry (`now = buf[i]`, `key = buf[i+1]` -- a fractional / epoch-ms `now` and a large
  key would box as plain arguments). `count(w?) -> number` is PURE (never mutates the rings; it only
  reads the oldest in-window entry per register), and runs Ertl's improved estimator (design-parity with lite-sketch,
  inline) -- standard error `1.04 / sqrt(m)` (guaranteed while `degraded === false`); `w` is an
  optional sub-window in `(0, W]` (outside that range -> NaN, never throws -- F12). `query()` aliases
  `count()`. Keys are safe integers; on add a bad key / now / option throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first
  (byte-identical no-op), while count(w) with a bad `w` reads NaN. Fully deterministic
  (no PRNG). Getters: `W` / `p` / `m` / `ringCap` / `seed` / `standardError` / `lastNow` / `mode` /
  `overflows` / `degraded` / `bytes`.
- `DriftDetector` -- class. A zero-GC, O(1)-STATE scalar streaming DRIFT DETECTOR over a
  real-valued signal (Page, Biometrika 1954; Mouss et al. 2004), selected by a mode const --
  `DRIFT_PH` (Page-Hinkley: cumulative deviation of x from the ONLINE running mean, two-sided) or
  `DRIFT_CUSUM` (two-sided CUSUM: two accumulators gP / gN each floored at 0, deviating from a FIXED
  `target` mu0). The mode is LOAD-BEARING via its REFERENCE: under a shared reference the two rules
  collapse to the identical reflected-random-walk statistic (CUSUM's max(0, cumsum) IS cumsum minus
  its running min -- what PH computes), so PH self-references the online mean (adaptive; it tracks a
  slow ramp and stays quiet) while CUSUM references a fixed mu0 (classic SPC; it fires whenever the
  signal departs mu0). `add(x) -> boolean` updates a running mean (Welford), runs the ONE mode
  branch, and returns true EXACTLY on the detecting item, RESETTING the accumulators + running mean
  so the NEXT shift is caught -- 0 B/op. The item-based, scalar, fixed-scalar-state complement to
  ADWIN's adaptive window: NO pool (pure scalars, like ForwardDecay), no window. Constructor
  `new DriftDetector(mode, { delta, threshold, target })` -- `delta` the magnitude allowance (PH) /
  slack (CUSUM), a finite number in [0, 1e150] (default 0.005; delta=0 is a VALID setting, guarded
  as `undefined`, never falsy); `threshold` the decision level (PH lambda / CUSUM decision interval),
  a finite number > 0 (default 50, tune to the signal scale); `target` the FIXED in-control mean mu0
  the CUSUM test deviates from, a finite number of ANY sign, |target| <= 1e150 (target=0 is valid) --
  REQUIRED for DRIFT_CUSUM, FORBIDDEN for DRIFT_PH (a mismatch throws [lite-adaptive], never a silent
  ignore). `add(x)` accepts a finite real with |x| <= DD_X_MAX (1e150, so the accumulators cannot
  overflow -- the ADWIN finite-overflow lesson); `addFrom(buf, i) -> boolean` is the zero-box sibling
  (reads `x = buf[i]` unboxed for a fractional x). `clear()` reuses the instance (keeps the config,
  incl. target). Getters: `mode` / `delta` / `threshold` / `target` (the fixed CUSUM mu0, `undefined`
  for PH) / `count` (items seen since the last reset) / `mean` (running mean) / `statistic` (the
  current test statistic, >= 0, crosses `threshold` exactly when `add` fires). `mean` / `statistic`
  throw [lite-adaptive] fail-closed on a non-finite accumulator; getters return 0 on empty. A bad
  mode / delta / threshold / target / option / x throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first (byte-identical
  no-op). DDM / EDDM (Bernoulli error-bit + tri-state output) are deliberately OUT of this class -- a
  future member.
- `SlidingDDSketch` -- class. A zero-GC WINDOWED relative-error QUANTILE summary over the LAST W
  (Masson-Rim-Lee, "DDSketch", VLDB 2019, over a fixed-(B+1) pane ring; ADR 0008) -- the recency sibling of
  lite-sketch's cumulative DDSketch and the quantile complement of SlidingHyperLogLog. A ring of B+1
  preallocated DDSketch panes (the `panes` option is B, the user knob), each covering W/B of the window;
  `add(now, value) -> this` (count mode via
  `add(undefined, value)`) bins the value on the SAME log scale (gamma = (1+alpha)/(1-alpha),
  key = ceil(log_gamma value), collapse-lowest default + strict opt-in) and writes the current pane,
  rotating + clearing panes as `now` advances -- 0 B/op incl. rotation. `addFrom(buf, i)` is the zero-box
  entry (`now = buf[i]`, `value = buf[i+1]` read UNBOXED). `quantile(q, w?) -> number` /
  `quantileInto(qs, out) -> count` / `count(w?) -> number` merge the live panes (INCLUDING the straddling
  oldest pane) into an INSTANCE-OWNED preallocated scratch (cold, 0 alloc) -- per-query relative error
  `<= alpha`; the covered span is [W, W + W/B]: the FULL window W, over-covered by at most one pane width
  W/B and never under-covered (disclosed + WITNESSED, since each pane collapses INDEPENDENTLY). `quantile`
  keeps ONE boxed return (16 B/call); `quantileInto` is 0 B/call (a render path). Value domain is positive
  + zero (negatives / out-of-indexable throw); a bad value / now / option throws [lite-adaptive]
  typeof-first (byte-identical no-op), but a bad query VALUE (q outside [0, 1] / NaN, or a `w` outside
  (0, W] / NaN) returns NaN, NEVER throws (null is not zero). Empty window -> NaN quantile / 0 count.
  Getters:
  `alpha` / `strict` / `panes` / `W` / `mode` / `lastNow` / `minIndexable` / `maxIndexable` / `collapsed`
  / `bytes`.
- `SlidingCountMin` -- class. A zero-GC WINDOWED per-label FREQUENCY summary over the LAST W
  (Cormode-Muthukrishnan, "Count-Min Sketch", 2005, over a fixed-(B+1) pane ring; ADR 0010) -- the
  recency sibling of lite-sketch's cumulative CountMinSketch and the frequency complement of
  SlidingHyperLogLog / SlidingDDSketch. A ring of B+1 panes, each a full d x w CountMin matrix covering
  W/B of the window; `add(now, key, count?) -> this` (count mode via `add(undefined, key, count?)`)
  hashes the key with the SAME two-lane murmur3 as lite-sketch CMS (base = hi ^ lo, row column =
  mix(base ^ i*ODD_CONST) & (w-1)) and writes the current pane's d cells (conservative-update PER PANE by
  default, plain add otherwise; saturating at 2^32-1), rotating + clearing panes as `now` advances --
  0 B/op incl. rotation. `addFrom(buf, i)` is the zero-box stride-3 entry (`now = buf[i]`, `key = buf[i+1]`,
  `count = buf[i+2]` read UNBOXED). `estimate(key, w?) -> number` SUMS each row's cell across the live panes
  then MINs over rows (sum-then-min); it returns a DOUBLE (a window sum can exceed 2^32) and NEVER throws
  (0 for an unseen but VALID key or an empty window; NaN for an out-of-domain key or a bad sub-window `w`
  -- F12: 0 was a fail-open under-count on an upper-bound sketch, and an invalid key was never seen 0
  times). The query covers the
  live panes so the span is [W, W+W/B]: the straddling oldest pane is KEPT, giving a ONE-SIDED upper bound
  true(W) <= est <= true(W+W/B) + epsilon*N. `advance(now)` / `advanceFrom(buf, i)` slide an idle window.
  Key domain: every SAFE INTEGER |key| <= 2^53 - 1 (so a composite channelIdx*2^32 + tag works for one
  shared instance); a bad key / count / now / option throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first on add / addFrom
  (byte-identical no-op), while estimate never throws (bad key / bad w -> NaN). Ctor `new SlidingCountMin(W, options?)` with
  `{ epsilon?, delta?, w?, d?, panes?, seed?, conservative? }` (epsilon -> w = ceil(e/epsilon) power-of-two,
  delta -> d = ceil(ln(1/delta)); explicit w / d override; defaults epsilon=delta=0.01 -> d=5, w=512,
  panes=32). No `merge` in 1.5.0. Getters: `d` / `w` / `panes` / `W` / `seed` / `conservative` / `saturated`
  (adds that hit the 2^32-1 ceiling -- the honesty flag) / `epsilon` / `delta` / `mode` / `lastNow` / `bytes`.
- `DecayedReservoir` -- class. A zero-GC RECENCY-BIASED fixed-k SAMPLE of actual stream values
  (Efraimidis-Spirakis A-Res weighted reservoir over ForwardDecay weights; ADR 0011) -- the sampling
  complement to `ForwardDecay`. An item's retention probability decays exponentially with its AGE
  (halves every `halfLife`), so the `k` retained values are always a decay-weighted sample of the
  recent stream. `add(now?, value?) -> this` (count mode via `add(undefined, value)`) draws ONE seeded
  xorshift32 uniform, forms an A-Res key in LOG SPACE (`log(u) * exp(-lambda*(t - L))` -- it underflows
  to 0 gracefully, never overflows), and sifts it into a size-`k` MIN-FOREST (design-parity with
  `HeavyKeeper` / lite-o1 `FreqO1`, inlined -- never a dep); amortized 0 B/op incl. the order-preserving
  landmark rebase (which never disturbs the retained set, so idle time needs no sweep). `addFrom(buf, i)`
  is the zero-box stride-2 entry (`now = buf[i]`, `value = buf[i+1]` read UNBOXED; EXPLICIT-time only).
  `value` is ANY finite real (signed OK; default 1). The caller reads the RAW sample:
  `sampleInto(buf) -> count` (0-alloc copy of the retained VALUES into a caller `Float64Array` of length
  `>= k`) and `forEach(fn)` (alloc-free `fn(value)`), then computes any statistic itself. It is a
  SAMPLE, not a hard window, so -- like `ForwardDecay` -- it has NO `advance()` (an idle stream
  correctly holds its last decayed sample). A bad `k` / `halfLife` / `seed` / `now` / `value` / buffer
  throws `[lite-adaptive]` typeof-first (a rejected add is a byte-identical no-op that does NOT advance
  the PRNG or the landmark). Deterministic given the seed. Getters: `k` / `halfLife` / `lambda` /
  `seed` / `size` / `mode` / `bytes`.
- `DRIFT_PH` / `DRIFT_CUSUM` -- the two DriftDetector mode consts (numeric, 0 / 1).
- `VERSION` -- string, '1.7.0'.

## ExponentialHistogram

    new ExponentialHistogram(W, epsilon, options?)

- W: window size; a finite number > 0 (items in count mode, or the `now`-unit span in
  explicit mode).
- epsilon: relative-error knob in (0, 1). Smaller -> more buckets -> tighter windowed
  error. `k = ceil(1/(2*epsilon)) + 1` buckets per level. The derived bucket-pool cap
  `(k+1)*levels + 2` is capped at 2^22 buckets (EH_CAP_MAX, ~150 MB at 36 B/bucket); a tiny
  epsilon past it throws a tagged RangeError BEFORE allocation instead of a V8 fatal (F11 --
  this rejects an epsilon below ~3e-6 at the default maxCount).
- options: `{ maxCount }`; an unknown key throws [lite-adaptive] with a did-you-mean hint (F13).
- maxCount: the window population the pool is GUARANTEED to hold, in EITHER mode -- a
  positive integer <= 2^53-1 (default 2^32). It sizes the fixed pool:
  `levels = max(2, ceil(log2(maxCount/(k+1))) + 2)`;
  `CAP = (k+1) * levels + 2` buckets (a fixed pool, never grows). The exact ceiling is
  `k * (2^levels - 1)` elements (>= maxCount, ~3-6x it; eps .01 + maxCount 5000 -> 26,061):
  the add past it (its merge cascade would pass the top level) throws a tagged RangeError
  (a byte-identical no-op).
  Pass `maxCount: W` in count mode to keep the pre-1.7.0 W-sized pool.
- Constructor throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first on a bad W / epsilon / maxCount /
  option BEFORE the pool is allocated (nothing half-built escapes).

Time modes (LOCKED at the first add, a switch throws [lite-adaptive]):

- EXPLICIT: add(now) / add(now, value). `now` is a finite number, strictly NON-
  DECREASING across calls (a decrease throws). The member never reads the wall clock.
- COUNT: add() / add(undefined, value). The member auto-increments an internal tick
  per add (the "last N items" convenience).

Hot surface (add is amortized O(1), zero allocation incl. the merge / expire reshaping):

- add(now?, value?) -> this   Open a bucket at `now` (or the auto-tick) with `value`
                              (default 1), run the bounded merge cascade, expire the
                              window edge. Fail closed: a mode switch, a non-finite /
                              decreasing `now`, or a non-positive value throws
                              [lite-adaptive] (typeof-first, BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this     The ZERO-BOX entry: read `now = buf[i]` and `value = buf[i+1]`
                              UNBOXED from a caller-owned PACKED [now, value] Float64Array
                              (a batch steps `i` by 2), then run the identical accumulate as
                              `add(now, value)`. For a caller whose `now` AND `value` are both
                              FRACTIONAL doubles (e.g. lite-hud's time-window sum/mean/rate):
                              `add` boxes each ~16 B HeapNumber at a non-inlined boundary; this
                              stays 0 B/op. EXPLICIT-time ONLY (a count-locked instance throws;
                              the first addFrom locks EXPLICIT). Same validation / throws /
                              byte-identical-no-op-on-reject; a bad buf/index throws typeof-first.
- advance(now) -> this        Move the window's reference time to `now` WITHOUT opening a bucket
                              (the R11 idle slide, ADR 0009): run add()'s expire sweep VERBATIM so
                              an idle stream still forgets at the edge and count()/sum() slide to 0.
                              EXPLICIT-time ONLY (count-locked throws, unset locks EXPLICIT),
                              monotone `now`; HOT, 0 B/op; a rejected advance is a byte-identical no-op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): `now = buf[i]` read UNBOXED
                              (needs `i < buf.length`), same mode / monotone / expiry, EXPLICIT-only.
- count() -> number           The windowed COUNT (population) over the last W. COLD,
                              O(levels). Relative error <= epsilon. Never throws (0 on empty).
- sum() -> number             The windowed SUM (of values) over the last W. COLD,
                              O(buckets). Never throws. ERROR (F17): absolute error
                              <= size(oldest straddling bucket)/2; relative <= epsilon
                              only for count / near-constant values (heavy-tailed / spiky
                              values can exceed it -- levels are sized by POPULATION, not
                              value mass). Use count() for a relative bound.
- query() -> number           The primary windowed estimate -- an alias of count(). COLD.
- clear() -> this             Reset to the empty window; reuse the pool (unlocks the mode).
- windowSize / epsilon        Getters: the window; the error knob.
- bucketCount / capacity      Getters: the live bucket count; the fixed pool capacity.
- k / levels                  Getters: the per-level bound; the number of size classes.
- maxCount (getter)           The declared (guaranteed) window population that sized the pool.
- mode (getter)               'unset' | 'explicit' | 'count' -- the locked time mode.

Recency contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives an evolving stream against an
exact ring-of-the-last-W oracle, measures the windowed COUNT relative error, and GATES it
`<= epsilon` on EVERY query across the W x epsilon sweep, plus a shifting-rate stream and
a dense 10 kHz / 70 s stream (F1: count() never NaN under the default maxCount); a broken
EH (no straddle half-correction) is REJECTED by the same gate. A separate SUM lane gates
the F17 bound `|sum_est - sum_true| <= size(straddling bucket)/2` on 100% of queries over
uniform / heavy-tail / spike streams and shows the old `sum <= epsilon` claim fails on
skew. Space co-headline: the fixed bucket pool vs the exact ring's O(W). The window is
HARD (EH forgets EXACTLY at the edge); the COUNT error is relative and hard (not statistical).

## ADWIN (ADR 0003)

    new ADWIN(delta, options?)

- delta: confidence knob in (0, 1). The stationary false-alarm rate is bounded by delta.
  Smaller -> fewer false alarms, longer detection latency.
- options: reserved object; an unknown key throws [lite-adaptive] with a did-you-mean hint (F13).
- Constructor throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first on a bad delta / option BEFORE the pool
  is allocated. The pool is FIXED at CAP = (M+1)*LEVELS + 2 = 386 buckets (M = 5, LEVELS =
  64) and never grows.

Item-indexed (NO clock): the adaptive window is measured in ITEMS, not time. `add(x)` takes
one finite real value per item (|x| <= sqrt(Number.MAX_VALUE)/2 ~= 6.7e153 since 1.7.0 -- the sums
are CENTRED on an offset c, and |x - c| <= 2*|x|max must still square finitely; a larger finite x
throws) and returns true iff a cut fired (drift detected) this add.

The ADWIN2 variance-aware cut: after the insert + merge cascade, every boundary split of
the window into W0 (older, n0 items) | W1 (newer, n1 items) is tested; a cut fires when
|mean(W0) - mean(W1)| > epsCut, where

    m       = 1 / (1/n0 + 1/n1)                          (harmonic mean of the sub-window counts)
    deltaP  = delta / ln(width)                          (Bifet-Gavalda multiple-testing correction)
    epsCut  = sqrt( (2/m) * sigmaHat^2 * ln(2/deltaP) ) + (2/3) * (R/m) * ln(2/deltaP)

sigmaHat^2 is the whole-window variance and R = max - min is the CURRENT window's range
(over the live buckets' per-bucket min/max, EXCLUDING the globally-oldest bucket -- since
1.7.0 F18; pre-1.7.0 R was a running global range over ALL x seen that never shrank, so ADWIN
went deaf to later shifts after one large level shift -- a straddling bucket pinned R). On a
detected cut the oldest bucket(s) are DROPPED (shrink W0 away) and the scan repeats until no
cut remains -- amortized O(1), 0 B/op incl. the cut-scan + shrink.

Hot surface:

- add(x) -> boolean           Append a finite real (|x| <= sqrt(Number.MAX_VALUE)/2), run the merge
                              cascade + the cut-scan, drop the older sub-window on a cut. Returns
                              true on the detecting item. Fail closed: a non-finite / non-number x,
                              or a finite |x| whose square would overflow, throws [lite-adaptive]
                              (typeof-first, BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op).
- clear() -> this             Reset to the empty window; reuse the pool.
- delta (getter)              The confidence knob.
- width (getter)             The current adaptive window size in items.
- mean / variance (getters)  The mean / variance over the current window (0 on empty).
- bucketCount / capacity      The live bucket count; the fixed pool capacity (386).

Change-response contract (the honesty anchor): the witness injects a known changepoint and
GATES the stationary false-alarm rate <= delta, a detection latency that scales with shift
magnitude, ~0 missed detections on a large shift, and adapted-window correctness (after a
cut the mean/width reflect the NEW concept only). Negative controls: a bound-disabled ADWIN
must false-alarm; a no-shrink ADWIN must fail to adapt -- both rejected by the same gates.

## ForwardDecay (ADR 0004)

    new ForwardDecay(halfLife, options?)

- halfLife: the decay half-life; a finite number > 0 (an element's weight halves over this
  span). lambda = ln2 / halfLife (getter `lambda`).
- options: reserved object; an unknown key throws [lite-adaptive] with a did-you-mean hint (F13).
- Constructor throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first on a bad halfLife / option BEFORE any
  field init. O(1) SPACE: two scalar accumulators C, Sv -- there is NO pool.

Model: exponential decay g(x) = exp(lambda*x) measured FORWARD from a fixed landmark L. Two
accumulators are maintained incrementally: C = sum g(t_i - L) (decayed count) and Sv = sum
value_i * g(t_i - L) (decayed weighted sum). A query at time `now` folds in the common age:

    decayedCount(now) = C  * exp(-lambda * (now - L))
    decayedSum(now)   = Sv * exp(-lambda * (now - L))
    mean(now)         = Sv / C                          (the age factor CANCELS -> now-invariant)
    rate(now)         = decayedCount(now) * lambda       (a DEFINITION: decayed events / unit time)

REBASE: when lambda*(t - L) would exceed FD_EXP_CAP = 40 (small on purpose: a single weight
stays <= exp(40) ~ 2.35e17, so the ACCUMULATOR sum has ~7.6e290x head-room under Double.MAX --
overflow needs a physically unreachable term count), `add` moves the landmark to t and rescales
C *= f; Sv *= f (f = exp(-lambda*(t - L))) -- EXACT modulo FP (it factors one common constant
out of every term). 0 B/op. The pathological tail (a single value within exp(40) of Double.MAX)
is caught FAIL-CLOSED: count/sum/mean/rate throw [lite-adaptive] on a non-finite accumulator.

Time modes (LOCKED at the first add, a switch throws [lite-adaptive]): EXPLICIT (add(now) /
add(now, value), `now` finite + non-decreasing) or COUNT (add() / add(undefined, value),
auto-tick). VALUE domain: ANY finite real (signed OK -- because C and Sv are separate, a
negative value lowers the decayed sum / mean but still counts as one decayed event; a
documented difference from EH's positive-only sum). Value defaults to 1.

Hot surface (add is O(1), 0 B/op incl. the rebase branch):

- add(now?, value?) -> this   Accumulate the forward-decayed weight (rebasing the landmark
                              if exp() would approach overflow). Fail closed: a mode switch,
                              a non-finite / decreasing `now`, or a non-finite value throws
                              [lite-adaptive] (typeof-first, BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this     The ZERO-BOX entry: read `now = buf[i]` and `value = buf[i+1]`
                              UNBOXED from a caller-owned PACKED [now, value] Float64Array
                              (a batch steps `i` by 2), then run the identical accumulate (incl.
                              the landmark rebase) as `add(now, value)`. For a caller whose `now`
                              AND `value` are both FRACTIONAL doubles (the lite-hud decayed-stats
                              idiom): `add` boxes each ~16 B HeapNumber at a non-inlined boundary;
                              this stays 0 B/op. EXPLICIT-time ONLY (a count-locked instance
                              throws; the first addFrom locks EXPLICIT + sets the landmark). Same
                              validation / throws / byte-identical-no-op-on-reject; a bad
                              buf/index throws typeof-first.
- count(now?) -> number       Decayed count at `now` (default = last add time). O(1).
- sum(now?) -> number         Decayed weighted sum at `now`. O(1).
- mean(now?) -> number        Decayed mean (Sv/C; landmark- and now-invariant). O(1).
- rate(now?) -> number        Decayed rate = decayedCount(now) * lambda (a definition). O(1).
- clear() -> this             Reset to empty; keep halfLife / lambda, unlock the mode.
- halfLife / lambda (getters) The decay half-life; the decay rate.
- landmark (getter)           The current landmark time L.
- mode (getter)               'unset' | 'explicit' | 'count'.

Query-now contract: an explicit query time must be a finite number >= the last add time (a
query in the PAST would un-decay -> throws [lite-adaptive]); in count mode queries take no
arg (use the internal tick). Queries never throw on empty (return 0) or a valid future now.

Exact-aggregate contract (the honesty anchor): the witness recomputes the decayed aggregate
directly from every stored (t_i, value_i) at each query time and GATES |fd - oracle| /
|oracle| <= 1e-9 on every query across 3 halfLife x 3 stream-shapes (>= 5000 queries).
Negative controls: fdNoRescale (rebase without the C,Sv rescale -> diverges) and fdNoRebase
(never rebases -> overflows to Inf) are both rejected by the same gate.

## HeavyKeeper (ADR 0005)

    new HeavyKeeper(d, w, k, options?)
    HeavyKeeper.withAccuracy(k, targetError, options?)   // static; derives d, w from k + error

- d: number of hash rows (~4-8). w: cells per row. k: the top-k size. options:
  `{ seed, b }` -- `seed` a Uint32 for the decay PRNG (default a fixed nonzero constant;
  seed=0 is valid), `b` the decay base (default ~1.08). A bad d / w / k / seed / b / option
  throws [lite-adaptive] typeof-first BEFORE any allocation. Memory caps are checked before
  allocation and throw a tagged RangeError naming the cap (F11): d*w <= 2^27 cells (HK_CELLS_CAP,
  ~1 GB at 8 B/cell), w <= 2^30 (HK_W_MAX), k <= 2^24 (HK_K_MAX, ~256 MB at 16 B/slot) -- an
  oversized table used to abort the process on a V8 fatal.
- add(key, weight = 1) -> this   HOT, amortized O(1), 0 B/op incl. the decay draw + the forest
                                 sift. `key` a SAFE INTEGER; `weight` an integer in [1, 2^32-1]
                                 (rank by count when 1, or by total time / bytes / any additive
                                 weight; a single over-range weight throws -- F10 -- while an
                                 ACCUMULATED cell SATURATES at 2^32-1, parity with SlidingCountMin).
                                 Hashes key to d cells (inline two-lane hash); a matching
                                 fingerprint += weight; a colliding one is DECAYED once with prob
                                 b^(-count) (seeded xorshift32), count -= weight (clamped), and
                                 the fingerprint is replaced when count hits 0. Fail closed: a
                                 non-safe-integer key, or a weight that is not an integer in
                                 [1, 2^32-1], throws [lite-adaptive] (byte-identical no-op).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX entry (F3 fixed): key = buf[i], weight =
                                 buf[i+1] read UNBOXED from a packed [key, weight] Float64Array.
                                 0 B/op for ALL safe-integer keys AND weights (incl. >= 2^31 and
                                 the default seed): the numeric inputs route through fixed module
                                 scratch slots, so nothing boxes at any call boundary. Plain
                                 add(largeKey) still boxes the key at the argument boundary (a ~16 B
                                 HeapNumber) -- use addFrom for large keys. Same validation + inline
                                 accumulate as add().
- estimate(key) -> number        COLD; the max matching cell count (0 for an unseen but VALID key;
                                 a non-safe-integer key -> NaN, never throws -- F12).
- forEach(fn) -> void            ALLOC-FREE iteration over the current top-k: fn(key, estimate).
                                 The render path (topK() may allocate; forEach never does).
- topKInto(buf) -> number        Pack the current top-k into a caller Float64Array as [key, estimate]
                                 pairs (2 floats per entry), 0-alloc; returns the entry count (<= k).
                                 buf must be a Float64Array of length >= 2*k, else it throws.
- topK() -> Array                COLD convenience; MAY allocate. Not for the hot/render path.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse the table + forest arrays).
- d / w / k / b / seed / bytes / size    Getters: the shape, the decay base, the PRNG seed, the
                                 fixed memory figure (bytes), and the live top-k size.

Top-k contract (the honesty anchor): the witness gates 100% RECALL of the true current top-k
above N/k vs an exact Map oracle (weighted AND unit streams), a BOUNDED ONE-SIDED error (each
reported total in [true - ~N/w, true], never over the truth), and the marquee claim -- MEASURED
mean rel-error over the true top-k LOWER than a faithful Space-Saving baseline (Metwally et al.
Stream-Summary) on a Zipfian + DRIFTING stream (measured 0.001% vs 36.75%). Negative controls
rejected by the same gate: a frozen-forest variant (recall 0%) and a decay-disabled variant
(b huge -> recall ~40% on drift). No `merge` (HeavyKeeper decays natively -- no rotation needed).
ADR 0005 records the weighted-miss decay rule (decay ONCE with prob b^(-count) then count -= weight;
per-weight-unit rejected as non-O(1)) and the seeded-PRNG choice.

## SlidingHyperLogLog (ADR 0006)

Windowed DISTINCT-count -- how many DISTINCT keys arrived in the LAST W, in FIXED preallocated
space at HLL accuracy (Chabchoub-Hebrail, "Sliding HyperLogLog", 2010). The RECENCY sibling of
lite-sketch's cumulative HyperLogLog: an `m = 2^p` register bank where each register, instead of a
single rho byte, keeps a small FIXED LFPM ring of `(timestamp, rho)` entries -- the List of Future
Possible Maxima, a per-register MONOTONIC DEQUE stored oldest -> newest with STRICTLY DECREASING
rho. An entry can be the window-max at some future time only if no NEWER entry has a >= rho (a
newer, larger-or-equal arrival dominates it forever, since it expires later); dominated entries are
dropped. Because a register's windowed max rho equals the HLL register of the in-window DISTINCT
key set (a duplicate never lowers a max), accuracy is the standard `1.04 / sqrt(m)` standard error
(gated at ~3 sigma), no extra bias -- guaranteed while `degraded === false`.

Constructor: `new SlidingHyperLogLog(W, options?)` where options = { p (int in [4, 16], default 10;
m = 1 << p), ringCap (a power of two in [2, 64], default 8; set >= q+1 to make overflow
impossible), seed (uint32, default 0x9e3779b1; seed=0 is a valid distinct seed -- guarded as
`undefined`, not falsy) }. A bad W / p / ringCap / seed / option throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor
door BEFORE any allocation.

- add(now, key) -> this          HOT, 0 B/op incl. the windowed eviction. EXPLICIT mode: a finite,
                                 non-decreasing `now`. COUNT mode: add(undefined, key) auto-ticks
                                 (W in items). The mode LOCKS at the first add (a switch throws).
                                 Inline two-lane murmur -> register + rho; pop dominated tail
                                 entries; append. A full ring drops its oldest entry and bumps
                                 overflows (degraded). Key is a safe integer; a bad key / now
                                 throws typeof-first (byte-identical no-op).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX: now = buf[i] (a fractional / epoch-ms
                                 double), key = buf[i+1] (a safe integer that may exceed 2^31),
                                 read UNBOXED. EXPLICIT-time only. Same validation + inline body
                                 as add().
- advance(now) -> this           Move the reference clock to `now` WITHOUT adding a key (the R11
                                 idle slide, ADR 0009). CLOCK-ONLY: set `_now`, touch NOTHING else --
                                 the PURE count() self-filters stamp <= now - W off `_now`, and
                                 expiring the ring here would perturb overflows/degraded (F8: the
                                 ring is only expired by add). EXPLICIT-time ONLY
                                 (count-locked throws, unset locks EXPLICIT), monotone; O(1), 0 B/op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this    The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): `now = buf[i]` read UNBOXED
                                 (needs `i < buf.length`), same clock-only body, EXPLICIT-only.
- count(w?) -> number            COLD, O(m). PURE (F8): NEVER mutates the rings (expiry lives in
                                 add). Read the oldest in-window entry per register (skips
                                 stamp <= now - w), run Ertl's improved estimator (sigma / tau,
                                 alpha_inf; inline). Returns 0 on an empty window. `w` is an
                                 optional sub-window in (0, W] (outside that range -> NaN, never
                                 throws -- F12).
- query() -> number              COLD; an alias of count() over the full window W.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse the arrays; unlocks the mode).
- W / p / m / ringCap / seed / standardError / lastNow / mode / overflows / degraded / bytes
                                 Getters: the shape, the seed, the theoretical standard error, the
                                 last applied time, the locked mode, the overflow count, the
                                 honest-degradation flag, and the fixed memory figure (bytes).

Windowed-distinct contract (the honesty anchor): the witness gates the relative error vs an EXACT
windowed-Set oracle at `3 * 1.04/sqrt(m)` on 100% of >= 2000 queries across a W-sweep + a
distinct-set shift + a post-burst edge, AND `degraded === false`. Negative controls rejected by
the same gate: a NO-EXPIRY variant (never drops stamp <= now - W -> stale keys counted forever)
and a NO-DOMINATED-DROP variant (a plain FIFO ring -> older high-rho maxima pushed out, wrong
register max). Memory `~ m * ringCap * 9 B` (Float64 stamp + Uint8 rho) + O(m) head/len; p=10,
ringCap=8 -> ~72 KB, never grows. ADR 0006 records the LFPM-ring-over-register-bank choice (vs the
rejected pane-rotation / full-HLL-pane alternatives), the Ertl estimator, the expiry rule
`stamp <= now - W`, and the ring-overflow-as-honest-degradation rationale.

## DriftDetector (ADR 0007)

Scalar, item-based, O(1)-STATE change detection over a real-valued signal (Page, "Continuous
Inspection Schemes", Biometrika 1954) -- "did the mean of THIS signal just shift?" in a handful of
scalars, no pool and no window (the lightest member; like ForwardDecay it keeps only scalars). The
cheap per-channel companion to ADWIN: where ADWIN keeps a variance-carrying bucket window and
auto-adapts its size, DriftDetector keeps a running mean plus one or two BOUNDED test accumulators
and returns true EXACTLY on the item that trips the threshold, then RESETS to catch the next shift.
A SINGLE class selects one of two classical tests via a mode const (exported alongside the class):

- DRIFT_PH -- Page-Hinkley (Page 1954; Mouss et al. 2004). Accumulates each x's deviation from the
  ONLINE running mean and watches the gap between the cumulative sum and its running extreme; a
  persistent one-directional drift makes the gap exceed the threshold lambda. Two-sided (an upward
  accumulator vs its running MIN, a downward one vs its running MAX). The online reference is
  ADAPTIVE -- it tracks a slow ramp and stays quiet.
- DRIFT_CUSUM -- two-sided CUSUM (Page 1954). Two accumulators, each FLOORED at 0, grow only while
  the signal departs a FIXED target mu0 by more than the slack delta; either exceeding the decision
  interval (threshold) fires. The fixed reference is the classic SPC in-control mean -- a SUSTAINED
  departure from mu0 keeps alarming (out-of-control); returning to mu0 quiets it.

The mode is LOAD-BEARING via its REFERENCE, not cosmetic: under a SHARED running-mean reference the
two rules collapse to the IDENTICAL reflected-random-walk statistic -- CUSUM's `max(0, cumsum)` is
exactly `cumsum` minus its running MIN, which is what Page-Hinkley computes explicitly. So they must
not share a reference: PH self-references the online mean (adaptive), CUSUM references a fixed mu0
(SPC). On a slow mean ramp they diverge sharply (PH quiet, CUSUM fires continuously) -- the witness
gates that divergence so a regression back to one statistic is rejected. (ADR 0007 records the
identity + the resolution.)

Constructor: `new DriftDetector(mode, options?)` where mode is DRIFT_PH or DRIFT_CUSUM (any other
value throws) and options = { delta (magnitude allowance / slack; a finite number in [0, 1e150],
default 0.005; delta=0 is a VALID setting, guarded as `!== undefined` not falsy), threshold (the
PH lambda / CUSUM decision interval; a finite number > 0, default 50), target (the FIXED in-control
mean mu0 the CUSUM test deviates from; a finite number of ANY sign, |target| <= 1e150, target=0
valid -- REQUIRED for DRIFT_CUSUM, FORBIDDEN for DRIFT_PH) }. A bad mode / delta / threshold /
target / option -- including a CUSUM without a target or a PH with one -- throws [lite-adaptive]
typeof-first BEFORE any field init (fail-closed, never a silent ignore).

- add(x) -> boolean         HOT, 0 B/op. Reject a non-finite x / a finite |x| > DD_X_MAX (1e150) on
                            the cold branch (byte-identical no-op), update the running mean (Welford),
                            run the ONE mode branch, and on a fire call the O(1) reset. Returns true
                            iff drift was detected on this item.
- addFrom(buf, i) -> boolean  HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX sibling: reads x = buf[i] UNBOXED from a
                            Float64Array (for a FRACTIONAL x that add(x) would box). Same validation
                            + body as add.
- clear() -> this           Reset all scalar state; keep the config (mode / delta / threshold /
                            target). O(1).
- mode / delta / threshold / target / count   Getters: the mode; the knobs; the fixed CUSUM mu0
                            (`undefined` for PH); items seen since the last reset.
- mean / statistic          Getters: the running mean; the current test statistic (>= 0, how close to
                            firing -- crosses threshold when add returns true). 0 on empty; THROW
                            [lite-adaptive] fail-closed if an accumulator ever went non-finite.

Fail-closed domain (the ADWIN finite-overflow lesson): DD_X_MAX = 1e150 caps |x| so the accumulators
can never be driven non-finite (each add moves them by ~2*DD_X_MAX; both bounded between resets;
reaching Double.MAX needs ~1e158 un-fired adds). delta is capped at the SAME bound -- each add also
moves the accumulators by ~delta, so an uncapped pathological delta would overflow them in a few adds
and add() would silently stop firing (a FAIL-OPEN boolean the getter guard cannot see). The
mean / statistic getters _guardFinite() as defense-in-depth. DDM / EDDM are OUT of this class (they
consume a Bernoulli error-bit stream + emit a tri-state stable/warning/drift output -- an
incompatible contract; a future member).

Change-response contract (the honesty anchor): the witness injects a known changepoint and GATES the
detection latency (a persistent shift above delta is detected) for BOTH modes + the stationary
false-alarm rate + reset discipline on a TRANSIENT shift (fire during the spike, go QUIET once the
signal returns to baseline) + the MODE-DIVERGENCE gate (on a slow ramp PH stays quiet while CUSUM vs
the fixed mu0 fires far more -- proving the mode is load-bearing). Negative controls REJECTED by the
same gates: a huge-threshold detector (never detects a real shift) and a no-reset variant (its
statistic stays latched and it keeps firing through the post-return tail of a transient). ADR 0007
records the PH+CUSUM-only roster choice (why DDM/EDDM were deferred), the running-mean-vs-fixed-target
reference distinction (and the cumsum-minus-running-min identity that forces it), the per-mode update
equations, the DD_X_MAX / delta / target overflow fail-closed argument, and the reset-on-detection
rationale.

## SlidingDDSketch (ADR 0008)

Windowed relative-error QUANTILES -- the p50 / p90 / p99 of the values in the LAST W, in FIXED
preallocated space with the SAME per-query bound as lite-sketch's cumulative DDSketch (Masson-Rim-Lee,
"DDSketch", VLDB 2019): `|q_est - q_true| <= alpha * q_true`. The recency sibling of cumulative DDSketch
and the quantile complement of SlidingHyperLogLog. It is the QUANTILE corner on the time axis.

Window model (ADR 0008, model A -- a fixed-(B+1) pane ring, F7): B+1 preallocated DDSketch panes (the
`panes` option is B, the user knob), each covering W/B of the window, held in a ring. add() writes the
CURRENT pane; when `now` crosses a pane boundary the ring rotates to the next pane and CLEARS it (fill(0),
0-alloc). A `now` jump of many pane-widths expires multiple panes in a bounded while-loop CAPPED at B+1
iterations (skipping >= B+1 panes clears the WHOLE ring, then re-anchors around `now`). quantile /
quantileInto / count MERGE the live panes (paneEnd > now - W, INCLUDING the straddling oldest pane) into
an INSTANCE-OWNED preallocated scratch (cold, 0-alloc -- NEVER a per-query allocation). The straddling
oldest pane is KEPT (never dropped), so the covered span is [W, W + W/B]: always the FULL window W,
over-covered by at most one pane width W/B and NEVER under-covered -- forgetting is at the far edge
[W, W + W/B], never before W. Dropping the oldest pane would under-count (the 1.6.0 B-pane ring did, and
under-reported the true count on 29410/29557 witness queries). Rejected alternatives: B (an EH/DGIM-style
histogram OF DDSketches -- merge-on-add allocates, not 0 B/op) and C (Arasu-Manku -- unbounded per-item
state, not zero-GC). Default panes B = 32 (edge over-coverage W/32; `panes` is a caller-tunable integer
in [2, 1024], and the ring holds B+1).

DDSketch mapping (INLINED, never an import -- a consumer like lite-hud pre-checks a value identically to
lite-sketch DDSketch, so a shared dependency's divergence would be a breaking surprise): gamma =
(1+alpha)/(1-alpha), key(x) = ceil(ln(x) * multiplier); x > 0 bins on the log scale, x === 0 routes to a
per-pane zero counter, x < 0 fails closed. Collapse-lowest by default (protects the p90/p99 tail);
`strict` opts into a fail-closed throw instead. The indexable band is computed with DDSketch's exact
ctor-time loop, so the ACCEPTED VALUE BAND is identical to lite-sketch DDSketch at every practical alpha.
SLD_KEY_MAX = 2^30 caps |key| fail-closed (per-pane offsets live in Int32Array; the ADWIN/DriftDetector
overflow lesson). SLD_MAX_BINS = 2048 (parity with lite-sketch DDSketch's default maxBins).

Strict mode (lite-sketch DDSketch parity, F2): `strict` never collapses. WITHOUT a `range` it is
SPAN-BASED -- a pane throws only when its OCCUPIED key span [minKeyPop, maxKeyPop] plus the new key would
exceed SLD_MAX_BINS; otherwise it RE-ANCHORS the window losslessly (shift the occupied bins down on a
key above the ceiling, up on a key below the floor). Span-based, NOT a bottom anchor -- a bottom anchor
would only move the bug to falling values (e.g. add(0,1); add(1,0.5)). WITH a declared `range` it is
DERIVED and FIXED: the bin offset is pinned at `rangeKeyLo = ceil(ln(rmin) * mult)`, nb = keyHi-keyLo+1
bins, never anchored to a first value, never slid, never collapsed; a value outside the band throws
"outside the declared strict range [rmin, rmax]" (a key-band check -- a value in rmin's / rmax's log
bucket is accepted, identical to lite-sketch). minIndexable / maxIndexable are ALPHA-ONLY: identical
across non-strict / strict / range.

Constructor: `new SlidingDDSketch(W, options?)` where options = { alpha (a number in (0, 1), default
0.01), strict (a boolean, default false -- null is not false), panes (an integer in [2, 1024], default
32), range ([rmin, rmax] with finite 0 < rmin < rmax, both inside the alpha indexable band and needing
<= SLD_MAX_BINS bins -> DERIVES strict) }. A declared `range` with `strict: false` is a contradiction and
throws. A bad W / alpha / strict / panes / range / option throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor door BEFORE
any allocation.

- add(now, value) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op incl. pane rotate + clear. EXPLICIT mode: a finite,
                                 non-decreasing `now`. COUNT mode: add(undefined, value) auto-ticks (W in
                                 items). The mode LOCKS at the first add. value >= 0 (negatives / out-of-
                                 indexable throw). Value + time validated BEFORE any state write (a reject
                                 is a byte-identical no-op); a strict-collapse reject throws before any
                                 bin write (time has legitimately advanced, state intact).
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX: now = buf[i], value = buf[i+1] read UNBOXED.
                                 EXPLICIT-time only. Same validation + body (duplicated) as add().
- advance(now) -> this           Move the window's reference time to `now` WITHOUT binning a value
                                 (the R11 idle slide, ADR 0009): rotate + clear stale panes via the
                                 private _advance so an idle stream slides to empty (count 0, quantile
                                 NaN). EXPLICIT-time ONLY (count-locked throws, unset locks EXPLICIT +
                                 anchors), monotone; bounded (<= panes clears), 0 B/op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this    The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): `now = buf[i]` read UNBOXED
                                 (needs `i < buf.length`), same rotate body, EXPLICIT-only.
- quantile(q, w?) -> number      COLD, 0 alloc apart from ONE boxed return (16 B/call -- use quantileInto
                                 on a render path). Merge the live panes into the scratch, walk it. NEVER
                                 throws on a bad VALUE: q outside [0, 1] / NaN, or `w` outside (0, W] /
                                 NaN / non-number -> NaN (null is not zero). NaN on an empty window. rel
                                 error <= alpha over the covered span [W, W + W/B].
- quantileInto(qs, out) -> count COLD, 0 B/call render (the cut lands in an instance scratch slot;
                                 _walkInto writes out[j] in place). merge ONCE, write each qs[j] -> out[j]
                                 (NaN for a bad q / empty window). Returns qs.length. A wrong CONTAINER
                                 type is a programming error: THROWS on non-Float64Array args or
                                 out.length < qs.length.
- count(w?) -> number            COLD, O(panes). Items in the last W (or sub-window w), incl. zeros. 0 on
                                 an empty window. NEVER throws on a bad VALUE: `w` outside (0, W] / NaN /
                                 non-number -> NaN (NaN, not 0 -- null is not zero).
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse the arrays; unlocks the mode).
- alpha / strict / panes / W / mode / lastNow / minIndexable / maxIndexable / rangeMin / rangeMax /
  collapsed / bytes             Getters: the knobs, the locked mode, the last applied time, the DDSketch
                                 indexable band, the declared strict range (NaN when undeclared), whether
                                 any live pane collapsed, the fixed memory figure.

Windowed-quantile contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives against an EXACT sorted-array oracle
over the sketch's LIVE pane content and gates rel error <= alpha on 100% of >= 2000 queries across 3 W x
3 alpha + a distribution SHIFT + a post-burst edge, AND asserts the TRUE-window gate: count >= true count
in (now - W, now] on 100% of the queries, with quantiles within alpha of the covered span [W, W + W/B].
Negative controls rejected by the same gates: a NO-EXPIRY variant (clear-on-rotate disabled -> stale
values linger -> rel >> alpha), a COARSE panes=2 variant (edge ~W/2, above the fine W/32 bound), and a
B-pane control (the 1.6.0 ring -- drops the straddling pane one pane width early and under-counts). Bin
counts are Uint32Array (saturate at 0xFFFFFFFF, never wrap -- the CountMinSketch precedent; the one
recorded deviation from lite-sketch DDSketch's Float64 bins), the merge scratch is Float64Array so B+1
near-saturated panes sum exactly to 2^53. Memory ~ (B+1) * 2048 * 4 B + scratch; panes=32 -> ~281 KB
(287949 B), never grows. ADR 0008 records the pane-ring choice (vs the rejected histogram-of-sketches / Arasu-Manku),
the rotate-and-clear model, the edge-error disclosure, the merge-into-instance-scratch 0-alloc argument,
the DDSketch mapping/collapse parity (and why inlined), the SLD_KEY_MAX overflow cap, and the
independent-pane-collapse subtlety (why the bound is witnessed, not assumed).

## SlidingCountMin (ADR 0010)

Windowed per-label FREQUENCY -- how many times did KEY occur in the LAST W, in FIXED preallocated space
with the SAME one-sided over-estimate as lite-sketch's cumulative CountMinSketch (Cormode-Muthukrishnan,
"Count-Min Sketch", 2005): est >= true(W), est - true <= epsilon*N w.p. >= 1 - delta. The recency sibling
of cumulative CountMinSketch and the frequency complement of SlidingHyperLogLog / SlidingDDSketch.

Window model (ADR 0010): B+1 panes, each a full d x w CountMin matrix covering W/B of the window, held in
a ring. add() writes the CURRENT pane; when `now` crosses a pane boundary the ring rotates to the next pane
and CLEARS it (fill(0), a bounded O(d*w) spike, disclosed as amortized). A `now` jump of k panes clears
min(k, B+1) panes, NEVER loops k (skipping >= B+1 panes clears them ALL, then re-anchors around `now`).
Panes are ABSOLUTELY grid-aligned (pane index = floor(now / paneWidth)) so two same-(W, panes) instances
would align (forward-compat for a future merge). The query covers the LIVE panes (paneEnd > now - W), so
the covered span is [W, W+W/B]: it ALWAYS covers the full W with at most one extra pane, and the partially-
expired oldest pane is KEPT, NEVER dropped -- so the estimate is a ONE-SIDED UPPER bound
true(W) <= est <= true(W+W/B) + epsilon*N(W+W/B). Dropping the oldest pane would under-count and silently
break the lower side of that contract.

CountMin mapping (INLINED, never an import -- a consumer swaps in lite-sketch CMS identically, so a shared
dependency's divergence would be a breaking surprise): the two-lane 64-bit murmur3 (hi, lo) over the key's
low + high words + sign, base = (hi ^ lo) | 0, and each of the d rows derives its column from ONE base lane
via `mix(base ^ i*ODD_CONST) & (w-1)` (w a power of two) -- byte-identical to lite-sketch CountMinSketch;
seed default shared with the hashing members, seed=0 valid (guarded via `=== undefined`, null is not zero).
Query estimate(key, w?): for each row SUM the key's cell across the live panes, THEN MIN over rows (sum-
then-min, NOT min-then-sum -- a windowed CMS must sum a row across time before taking the row-min). Counters
are per-pane Uint32Array, SATURATING at 2^32-1 (never wrap; the `saturated` getter is the honesty flag, like
SlidingHLL's `degraded`). Conservative update (default) runs PER PANE (min over the current pane's d cells),
NOT over window sums. W is a finite number > 0 with NO small cap (parity with SlidingDDSketch /
SlidingHyperLogLog -- the cell array (B+1)*d*w is INDEPENDENT of W); the 1<<16-style cap is on the WIDTH w
(cells/row, tighter than lite-sketch's 1<<25 because the store is B+1 full matrices), and d (rows) is capped
at 32 (D_MAX). Rejected alternative (ADR 0010): an EH-per-cell ECM-sketch (Papapetrou et al., VLDB 2012) --
one exponential histogram PER counter cell gives a tighter per-cell error but ~6 MB and a variable-cost
merge-on-add, not the 0 B/op the suite sells.

Constructor: `new SlidingCountMin(W, options?)` where options = { epsilon (a number in (0, 1), default 0.01
-> w = ceil(e/epsilon) rounded up to a power of two), delta (a number in (0, 1), default 0.01 -> d =
ceil(ln(1/delta))), w (explicit width in [1, 2^16], overrides epsilon), d (explicit depth in [1, 32],
overrides delta), panes (B; an integer in [2, 1024], default 32 -- the ring holds B+1), seed (uint32, any
integer, default shared), conservative (a boolean, default true -- null is not true) }. Defaults ->
d=5, w=512, panes=32 -> ~338 KB. A bad W / epsilon / delta / w / d / panes / seed / conservative / option
throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor door BEFORE any allocation. No `merge` in 1.5.0 (deferred).

- add(now, key, count?) -> this  HOT, 0 B/op incl. pane rotate + clear. EXPLICIT mode: a finite,
                                 non-decreasing `now`. COUNT mode: add(undefined, key, count?) auto-ticks
                                 (W in items). The mode LOCKS at the first add. key a SAFE INTEGER
                                 (|key| <= 2^53 - 1); count a positive integer in [1, 2^32-1] (default 1).
                                 Key + count + time validated BEFORE any state write (a reject is a byte-
                                 identical no-op). Conservative update per pane by default; saturating.
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX stride-3: now = buf[i], key = buf[i+1],
                                 count = buf[i+2] read UNBOXED. EXPLICIT-time only. Same validation + body
                                 (duplicated) as add().
- estimate(key, w?) -> number    COLD, O(d x (B+1)). SUM each row's cell across the live panes,
                                 then MIN over rows. Returns a DOUBLE (a window sum can exceed 2^32). NEVER
                                 throws: 0 for an unseen but VALID key or an empty window; NaN for an
                                 out-of-domain key or a bad sub-window w (F12: 0 was a fail-open under-count
                                 on an upper-bound sketch, and an invalid key was never seen 0 times). `w` an
                                 optional sub-window in (0, W]. ALLOC (F6): a windowed count >= 2^31 boxes ONE
                                 ~16 B HeapNumber per call at a non-inlined call site (the honest return of a
                                 large double); a count < 2^31 is a Smi, 0 B/call. The 1.8.0 `estimateInto`
                                 slot reader is the 0-alloc render path.
- advance(now) -> this           Move the window's reference time to `now` WITHOUT adding (the R11 idle
                                 slide, ADR 0009): rotate + clear stale panes via the private _advance so
                                 an idle stream slides to empty (estimate 0). EXPLICIT-time ONLY (count-
                                 locked throws, unset locks EXPLICIT + anchors), monotone; bounded
                                 (<= B+1 clears), 0 B/op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this    The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): `now = buf[i]` read UNBOXED (needs
                                 `i < buf.length`), same rotate body, EXPLICIT-only.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse the arrays; unlocks the mode).
- d / w / panes / W / seed / conservative / saturated / epsilon / delta / mode / lastNow / bytes
                                 Getters: the shape, the seed / mode knobs, the saturation honesty flag,
                                 the theoretical error e/w and failure e^-d, the locked mode, the last
                                 applied time, the fixed memory figure.

Windowed-frequency contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives against an EXACT per-key ring oracle
and gates the ONE-SIDED bound true(W) <= est <= true(W+W/B) + epsilon*N on 100% of >= 2000 queries across
>= 4 (W, eps) pairs + a churny key stream + advance-empties. Negative controls rejected by the same gate: a
DROP-OLDEST-PANE variant (under-counts -> breaks the lower bound est >= true(W)) and a MIN-THEN-SUM variant
(min over rows per pane, then sum -> wrong). Memory ~ (B+1) * d * w * 4 B + paneEnd + scratch; defaults ->
~338 KB, never grows. ADR 0010 records the B+1 / keep-oldest one-sided-bound rationale, the rejected ECM-
sketch alternative, the absolute pane alignment, sum-then-min, per-pane conservative update, Uint32
saturation + `saturated`, the W-not-capped resolution, and the lite-sketch byte-parity note.

## DecayedReservoir (ADR 0011)

A recency-biased fixed-k SAMPLE of ACTUAL stream values -- the "give me k real recent items" member.
Where the other members each answer ONE pre-decided question (a count, a distinct, a quantile, a
frequency), a reservoir hands the caller `k` retained values from which they compute ANYTHING (any
quantile, any custom function), approximately. The sampling complement to `ForwardDecay`: FD gives
decayed AGGREGATES exactly (two scalars), DecayedReservoir gives a decayed SAMPLE (k slots). It is the
SAMPLE corner on the time axis.

Algorithm (ADR 0011): Efraimidis-Spirakis A-Res weighted reservoir sampling (Efraimidis-Spirakis,
"Weighted random sampling with a reservoir", 2006) with FORWARD-DECAY weights (Cormode et al., ICDE
2009 -- the same decay model as `ForwardDecay`). Each accepted item draws ONE uniform u in (0, 1) from
a seeded xorshift32 (the exact `HeavyKeeper` derivation, so seed=0 is a valid distinct seed) and forms
an A-Res key. The textbook key is `u^(1/w)` with weight `w = exp(lambda*(t - L))`; DecayedReservoir
works it in LOG SPACE -- `key = log(u) * exp(-lambda*(t - L)) * _scale` -- which is numerically STABLE
(`exp(-lambda*age)` underflows to 0 gracefully as age grows, instead of `exp(+...)` overflowing to
Inf). The k highest keys are kept in an intrusive size-k MIN-FOREST (design-parity with `HeavyKeeper` /
lite-o1 `FreqO1`, inlined -- never a dep): a new item whose key beats the forest root replaces it and
sifts down. Because recent items get keys nearer 0 (the top), they are more likely retained -- the
decay bias. The value column stores the payload alongside its key.

Landmark rebase (order-preserving, the key subtlety): as `t` advances from the landmark `L`,
`exp(-lambda*(t - L))` shrinks toward 0. When `lambda*(t - L)` exceeds `DR_EXP_CAP = 40` the landmark
rebases to `t` and a single scalar `_scale` absorbs the common factor -- this multiplies EVERY stored
key by the same positive constant, a MONOTONE transform, so the retained-set membership and the forest
order are UNCHANGED (no per-slot sweep; 0 B/op). A very large idle gap then a resume is capped at
`DR_F_CAP = 700` on the rebase-factor argument so a key can never underflow to -0 and tie the whole
forest (the ADWIN/FD/SLD overflow lesson, on the sampling axis). Because decay is applied at INSERT
and membership is fixed thereafter, an idle stream correctly HOLDS its last decayed sample -- there is
nothing to "slide to empty", so (like `ForwardDecay`) DecayedReservoir has NO `advance()`.

Constructor: `new DecayedReservoir(k, halfLife, options?)` where `k` is a positive integer (the sample
size, a positive integer <= 2^24 -- DR_K_MAX, ~256 MB at 16 B/slot; a bigger k throws a tagged
RangeError BEFORE allocation instead of a lazy multi-GB over-commit, F11), `halfLife` a finite number
> 0 (`lambda = ln2 / halfLife`), options = { seed (uint32, default 0x9e3779b1; seed=0 valid, guarded
as `undefined`) }. A bad k / halfLife / seed / option throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor door BEFORE
any allocation.

- add(now?, value?) -> this      HOT, amortized 0 B/op incl. the PRNG draw + forest sift + rebase.
                                 EXPLICIT mode: a finite, non-decreasing `now`. COUNT mode:
                                 add(undefined, value) auto-ticks. The mode LOCKS at the first add (a
                                 switch throws). `value` is ANY finite real (signed OK), default 1.
                                 Value + now + mode are validated FIRST -- a reject is a byte-identical
                                 no-op that does NOT advance the PRNG or the landmark.
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX stride-2: now = buf[i], value = buf[i+1] read
                                 UNBOXED from a packed [now, value] Float64Array. EXPLICIT-time only.
                                 Same validation + body as add.
- sampleInto(buf) -> number      COLD, 0 alloc. Copy the current retained VALUES into a caller
                                 Float64Array (length must be >= k, else throws); returns the count
                                 written (`size`, <= k). Order is heap order, NOT sorted.
- forEach(fn) -> void            Alloc-free iteration over the current sample: fn(value). A non-function
                                 fn throws [lite-adaptive] before iteration.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse both columns; unlock the mode; replay the PRNG
                                 from its seeded initial state -- a cleared reservoir replays identically).
- k / halfLife / lambda / seed / size / mode / bytes   Getters: the sample size, the decay knob,
                                 ln2/halfLife, the PRNG seed, the live sample size, the locked mode, and
                                 the fixed memory figure (`k * 16 + 64` bytes: two Float64 columns + scalars).

Recency-sample contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives an evolving stream over many
independent seeds and gates that the sample's empirical INCLUSION RATE as a function of item AGE
decays as `exp(-lambda*age)` (recent items over-represented by exactly the decay factor), within a
stated statistical band. Negative controls REJECTED by the witness: a NO-DECAY reservoir (a plain
uniform draw -> flat inclusion rate, rejected by the slope fit) and a NO-FOREST reservoir (keep the
first k forever -> recent items never sampled, rejected because its newest-age inclusion rate is ~0).
A long-idle-then-resume lane asserts the sample stays
well-defined (no NaN, no ambiguous ties, membership deterministic across seeds). ADR 0011 records the
A-Res + log-space-forward-decay-key choice, the order-preserving-rebase proof, the seeded-PRNG choice,
the advance()-excluded rationale, the raw-sample-only surface, the min-forest reuse, and the rejected
alternatives (A-ExpJ skip-sampling; a hard-window sample; bundled convenience aggregates).

## advance() / idle-slide (ADR 0009)

R11: a sliding-window summary must be able to slide even when NO data arrives. Without it, an
idle stream reports a STALE window -- count()/sum()/quantile() keep returning last-second values
long after the window should have emptied, because the members only expire ON an add(). v1.4.0
adds `advance(now)` / `advanceFrom(buf, i)` to the three TIME-windowed members so the caller can
move the window forward with no traffic.

- advance() moves the window's reference time forward and applies the SAME expiry / rotation an
  add would, WITHOUT inserting a value. Queries stay PURE (they never mutate); advance() is the
  only op that moves the clock without a value.
- Per-member body: ExponentialHistogram runs add()'s expire loop VERBATIM (opens no bucket).
  SlidingHyperLogLog is CLOCK-ONLY (set `_now`; count() skips stamp <= now - W as a PURE read,
  and the next add drops expired heads -- 1.7.0 F8 -- so overflows/degraded never depend on how
  often count() or advance() is called). SlidingDDSketch
  rotates + clears stale panes via the private `_advance` (bounded, <= panes clears).
- Mode rule (all 3, parity with addFrom): EXPLICIT-time ONLY. A COUNT-locked instance throws; an
  UNSET instance locks EXPLICIT (and anchors, for SlidingDDSketch). Monotone: `now` finite and
  >= lastNow (a decrease throws). A rejected advance is a BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op. All 0 B/op.
- EXCLUDED: ForwardDecay (satisfies R11 already via its now? query args -- decay is computed at
  query time relative to `now`, so an idle FD already fades correctly with no advance needed);
  ADWIN, HeavyKeeper, DriftDetector (item-indexed, NOT time-windowed -- they have no `now` axis
  to advance).
- Every existing method + hot body of the three touched classes is BYTE-IDENTICAL; advance /
  advanceFrom are pure additions.

## Query allocation -- the render path (F6)

One rule: a query that RETURNS a fractional or large double boxes ONE ~16 B HeapNumber per call
at a non-inlined call site; the `xxxInto` / `forEach` readers are the 0-alloc render path. So on a
10-15 Hz render loop use `SlidingDDSketch.quantileInto` (0 B/call) not `quantile` (16 B/call), and
`HeavyKeeper.forEach` / `topKInto` (0 B/call) not `topK`. `SlidingCountMin.estimate` boxes 16 B/call
only when the windowed count is >= 2^31 (a Smi-range count returns 0 B/call; the 1.8.0 `estimateInto`
is the slot reader that fixes it). `ExponentialHistogram.sum()` and `HeavyKeeper.estimate` box only in
the early JIT tier (steady state 0). `count()` and integer-count returns are Smis, 0 B/call.

## The time source + the bucket pool (ADR 0001)

A caller-supplied MONOTONE `now` (logical tick or ms; count-mode convenience when
omitted); the member never reads the wall clock (deterministic, testable). A fixed,
preallocated bucket pool over a Struct-of-Arrays (Float64 timestamp / earliest-time /
size, Int32 per-level linkage + free-list) with no per-op allocation -- the lite-o1
fixed-capacity zero-GC discipline on the recency axis. ADR 0002 records the EH merge /
expire / query + the error bound + the DGIM note + the mode-lock; ADR 0003 the ADWIN2
variance-aware cut + the adaptive shrink; ADR 0004 the ForwardDecay landmark rebase
(exact modulo FP), the FD_EXP_CAP=40 bounded-accumulator + fail-closed-query argument, the signed-value call, and the
rate()=count*lambda definition. ForwardDecay keeps NO pool (two scalar accumulators).

## Scripts

- npm test          -- node:test behavioral + fail-closed suite
- npm run witness   -- the recency witness (windowed error vs the epsilon bound + negative control)
- npm run torture   -- the 0 B/op leak + GC-profiler gate on add incl. reshaping (node --expose-gc)
- npm run test:perf -- flat-throughput perf gate + a must-allocate control
- npm run test:types-- the ambient type-surface compile check
- npm run verify    -- test + test:types + torture + witness + test:perf (the release gate)

## Roadmap

ExponentialHistogram (0.1.0, sliding-window count / sum) -> ADWIN (0.2.0, drift +
adaptive window) -> ForwardDecay (0.3.0, time-decayed aggregates) -> HeavyKeeper
(0.4.0, decayed / windowed heavy hitters) -> 1.0.0 (API freeze -- the four-member roster
is COMPLETE, no new member; a docs / stability milestone) -> 1.1.0 (SlidingHyperLogLog --
windowed distinct-count; the FIRST additive post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.2.0 (DriftDetector
-- scalar Page-Hinkley / CUSUM change detection; the SECOND additive post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND)
-> 1.3.0 (SlidingDDSketch -- windowed relative-error quantiles; the THIRD additive post-1.0 member, a
PURE APPEND) -> 1.4.0 (the R11 advance() / advanceFrom() idle-slide sweep on the three TIME-windowed
members -- ExponentialHistogram, SlidingHyperLogLog, SlidingDDSketch; additive, existing methods
byte-identical) -> 1.5.0 (SlidingCountMin -- windowed per-label frequency; the FOURTH additive post-1.0
member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.6.0 (DecayedReservoir -- recency-biased fixed-k sample; the FIFTH additive
post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.7.0 (the H1 HARDENING release: in-place fixes across members
from the 1.6.0 final-sweep audit -- NOT a pure append; see CHANGELOG 1.7.0). The 1.6.0 member
COMPLETES the confirmed post-1.0 roadmap. The one remaining
optional / unscheduled tail member is an error-rate DDM / EDDM detector (Bernoulli error-bit stream ->
stable / warning / drift) -- built on demand if a consumer asks; it would be a pure append that keeps
the frozen core byte-identical.
